title: A Cavity-Interfaced Register of Trapped-Ion Qubits with Multi-Second Coherence
authors: James Bate, Johannes Helgert, Marco Canteri, Victor Krutyanskiy, Benjamin Peter Lanyon
abstract: Scalable quantum networks require generating remote entanglement faster than decoherence erases it, calling for nodes that combine efficient light-matter interfaces with long coherence times. Cavity-coupled trapped ions are a promising platform for network nodes, offering high-efficiency extraction of photons. Here, we report multi-second coherence for a qubit register in a cavity-integrated ion trap. First, using dynamical decoupling on spin ground states, the coherence times of five co-trapped ion qubits are extended into the multi-second regime. Second, cavity-collected ion-photon entanglement is faithfully stored in these protected ion-memory states for multiple seconds. Third, we show that ion-memory qubits can be robust to the generation over a thousand cavity photons by a co-trapped ion, with decoherence limited by laser crosstalk. Finally, we estimate that a modestly improved and duplicated ion-cavity system could enable the simultaneous establishment of multiple remote Bell pairs between two remote ion registers, representing a step toward networking multi-qubit prototype trapped-ion quantum processors.
summary: This paper reports on the creation of a highly coherent quantum node using trapped ions coupled to an optical cavity. By implementing dynamical decoupling, the researchers extended qubit coherence to multiple seconds, and successfully stored ion-photon entanglement for extended periods. This work represents a significant step toward building scalable, multi-qubit quantum processors and quantum networks.
main_problem: Developing scalable quantum networks requires generating remote entanglement faster than decoherence erases it, necessitating quantum nodes with efficient light-matter interfaces and long coherence times.
main_result: The authors demonstrated multi-second coherence times for a register of up to five trapped-ion qubits and achieved ion-photon entanglement coherence times significantly longer than previous reports.
method: The study utilized dynamical decoupling sequences (like XY16) on trapped ions coupled to an optical cavity to protect quantum information and generate entanglement with photons.
model_or_system: The physical system is a cavity-coupled ion trap, using trapped $\text{Ca}^+$ ions as qubits. Qubits are encoded in metastable Zeeman states, and the system leverages strong ion-cavity coupling for high-efficiency photon extraction.
key_observables: Single-qubit process fidelities, ion-photon entanglement fidelity ($F_B$), and coherence time ($\tau$).
important_parameters: Multi-second coherence times ($\tau \approx 65\text{s}$ for single qubits), cavity coupling strength ($g_0 = 2\pi \times 1.53 \text{ MHz}$), and the number of co-trapped ions (up to five).
main_assumptions: The coherence is limited by laser crosstalk, and the final networking capability relies on estimations for an improved and duplicated system.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the energy level diagram and setup schematic. Figure 2 illustrates single-qubit process fidelities vs. storage time for one and five ions. Figure 3 shows the measured ion-photon entanglement fidelity vs. time.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for long-coherence quantum nodes. It then details the experimental realization, demonstrating multi-second coherence using dynamical decoupling. Subsequently, it measures and reports the fidelity of stored ion-photon entanglement, concluding with estimates for scaling to multi-remote-pair generation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the core challenge of quantum networking—maintaining entanglement coherence over time—by combining advanced quantum memory techniques (dynamical decoupling) with high-fidelity light-matter interfaces (cavity QED).

(b) Schematic of five co-trapped 40Ca+ ions (trap electrodes not shown). A cavity photon is generated from ion 1 via a focused 393 nm Raman pulse. The remaining ions serve as quantum memories, with qubits encoded in the ground-state spin lev- els (|S⟩/|S′⟩). The cavity mode has a waist of 12.0 µm. The shown ion separations are symmetric around ion 3.

FIG. 2. Memory qubit coherence enhanced by dynamical decoupling. Process fidelities with the ideal identity opera- tor versus storage time for (a) one and (b) five co-trapped ions. Filled shapes: data; error bars represent one standard deviation of statistical uncertainty, derived from Monto Carlo analysis of tomographic data. Grey solid lines: fits to Eq. 1 in the main text. Black dashed lines show the 0.5 fidelity thresh- old for storage of remote entanglement. Inset (a): single-ion performance without spin echoes; blue line: model of 50 Hz magnetic-field noise.
